depth_justification: Genuinely engages Anchor's specifics (employer/insurer fear, substance-use as special-category data, opt-in clinic integration, relapse-score psychological harm, low-literacy DE/FR/IT/EN) with many correct precise citations (GDPR Art. 9(2)(a), 32, 33/34, 44-49; ePrivacy 5(3)), but is badly undermined by repeating the same multi-dimension analysis block verbatim across three turns, fabricated/generic dimension IDs (P1.D1..P7.D1), and a couple of wrong cites (Art. 30 used for security/DPIA, Art. 22 for multilingual).
actionability_justification: The final severity-grouped report pairs each risk with a concrete, implementable mitigation and the relevant standard (E2EE for health data, SCCs for cross-border transfers, OAuth 2.0 secure APIs, an Art. 33/34 breach-response plan, high-contrast/icons/large fonts for low-literacy), though a few items stay directional ('conduct bias audits').
salient_examples: Implement end-to-end encryption for all health data, including relapse-risk scores and substance logs. | GDPR Article 32, ISO 82304-2
secure APIs and authentication mechanisms (e.g., OAuth 2.0) to protect data integrity
ASSISTANT block 'HERA Dimension: Data Protection & Privacy [P3.D1] ... [P7.D1]' repeated verbatim across consecutive turns
Multilingual support (DE, FR, IT, EN) aligns with GDPR Article 22 (non-discrimination)
